source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can two interfaces using the same language model support different actions?

options.text: Their product labels specify which file operations the model can perform.
options.feedback: A product label is insufficient evidence of available actions. Inspect the actual tools and permissions supplied by the environment.

options.text: Their models execute file operations directly after describing them.
options.feedback: A model generates a request; execution happens through the harness and an available tool. A description alone does not perform the operation.

options.text: Their harnesses can supply different tools and execution permissions.
options.feedback: Sharing a model does not imply sharing its operating environment. The harness and tools determine which supported requests can actually run.

options.text: Their project names determine the operations built into the model weights.
options.feedback: Project selection gives the agent relevant context and a place to work. It does not change model weights to provide file operations.
